mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 3 months (measured as the 3-month change) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The decline must be at least 0.2 percentage points to be considered significant.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where UNRATE declines by at least 0.2pp over 3 months are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past 3 months signals a tightening monetary cycle combined with economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The rise must exceed 0.2pp for FEDFUNDS and 0.1pp for UNRATE.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and UNRATE rises > 0.1pp over 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp and UNRATE rises > 0.1pp over 3 months are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3% year-over-year), the S&P 500 tends to have negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to central bank tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 450,000 units, it signals a demand slowdown that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where HOUST < 450 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months (measured as the 3-month change) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The decline must be at least 0.5% to be considered significant.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% over 3 months are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in CPIAUCSL above 215 (current value 212.174) signals inflationary pressure that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to short-term risk-off sentiment.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods where CPIAUCSL > 215 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and fall in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals a supply-demand mismatch that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The rise must exceed 0.5% for INDPRO and the fall must exceed 5% for HOUST.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 0.5% and HOUST falls > 5% over 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO rises > 0.5% and HOUST falls > 5% over 3 months are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
